page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. The system achieves top 10% placement in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, Passmark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks. It also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in static web serving throughput, Redis SET operations, and software compilation. Single-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, though single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores remain in the average range.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and DDR5 memory speeds, this instance is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads requiring massive resource density without the overhead of local storage or GPU hardware. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and LLM prompt processing. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and weak text generation speeds for small LLM models represent key architectural tradeoffs to consider.
